Week 10: MOATS

Econ 238, Fall 2026. Notice card, audio discussion, and group notes.

The Notice card

NOTICE!

South Burlington keeps its woods

What we do: Keep about 1,000 acres of the Southeast Quadrant closed to development, and steer new housing into City Center, the downtown we are still building.

What pushes back: Developers, housing advocates, and our own economic development committee, who argued the rules would erode the tax base and raise housing costs. One developer sued.

The cost you can see: Legal fees and land value owners can’t cash in. The cost you can’t: every home not built here pushes up rents and lengthens commutes, paid by renters and newcomers. That hidden cost is probably the larger one.

Be honest about it: This is a boundary as much as a conservation policy. It protects woods, and it also keeps people out.

If the woods belong to everyone, who actually gets to live next to them?
